description: Scenario contract for the NULQ vulnerable-target laboratory. Supported scenarios are evaluated against the real binary's JSON. Unsupported scenarios document checks that cannot run in this container and are never reported as passes.

scenarios.title: World-writable directory without sticky bit detected
scenarios.description: fs/world-writable (0777, no sticky) must produce a NULQ-FS-002 MEDIUM finding.

scenarios.title: Sticky-bit world-writable directory is not itself escalated
scenarios.description: fs/world-writable-sticky (1777) must not produce a NULQ-FS-002 finding (sticky bit prevents escalation).

scenarios.title: Root-owned SUID executable inventory
scenarios.description: suid/root-owned-tool (4755, root:root) must produce a NULQ-FS-001 LOW finding (privileged executable outside standard system directories).

scenarios.title: SUID in world-writable directory escalates to HIGH
scenarios.description: sgid/writable-dir/suid-tool (root SUID inside 0777 dir) must produce a NULQ-FS-002 HIGH finding on the directory.

scenarios.title: Inert SUID without execute bit is INFO
scenarios.description: suid/inert-suid (4644, no exec bit) must produce INFO, never HIGH (set-owner-ID bit without execute bit is inert).

scenarios.title: World-writable directory with root-owned executable
scenarios.description: fs/world-writable-exec (0777 dir containing root-owned non-SUID executable) produces MEDIUM, not HIGH (no directly replaceable privileged executable).

scenarios.title: Writable parent directory ancestry
scenarios.description: fs/writable-parent (0777 parent with child tool) produces MEDIUM on the parent directory.

scenarios.title: Unsafe directory ancestry attributed to directly writable directory
scenarios.description: fs/ancestry (nested 0777 directories with tool at leaf) attributes the finding to the directly writable directory containing the executable, with MEDIUM severity.

scenarios.title: Sticky-bit owned-by-user edge case
scenarios.description: fs/sticky-owned (1777 owned by vulntarget user, containing root SUID tool) is replaceable by that user and produces HIGH.

scenarios.title: Clean directory negative control
scenarios.description: fs/clean (0755, root-owned, plain file) must produce no NULQ-FS-002 finding.

scenarios.title: Unreadable subtree reported as partial coverage
scenarios.description: permissions/denied (0700, root-owned) must be reported as permission-denied in coverage, not silently skipped.

scenarios.title: Writable PATH directory detected as LOW
scenarios.description: path/writable (0777) in PATH must produce a NULQ-FS-003 LOW finding.

scenarios.title: Late-writable PATH entry is LOW not HIGH
scenarios.description: path/late-writable (0777 after /usr/bin) must produce LOW, not HIGH (no privileged consumer observed).

scenarios.title: Symlink PATH entry resolved to safe target
scenarios.description: links/path-link (symlink to non-writable path/safe) must not produce a PATH finding (resolved target decides permissions).

scenarios.title: Empty PATH entry detected
scenarios.description: PATH contains an empty entry (double colon) which NULQ-FS-003 reports.

scenarios.title: Wheel supplementary group membership
scenarios.description: The assessment account (uid 10001) is granted wheel (gid 10) at runtime; NULQ-ID-001 must report privileged group membership as LOW.

scenarios.title: SGID executable inventory
scenarios.description: sgid/sgid-tool (2755, root:wheel) must produce a NULQ-FS-001 LOW finding (privileged executable outside standard system directories).

scenarios.title: Non-privileged executable with wrong ownership is not flagged
scenarios.description: app/tool owned by 10002:10002 but not SUID/SGID must not produce a NULQ-FS-001 finding (not a privileged executable).

scenarios.title: Writable application configuration directory
scenarios.description: app/config/writable (0777) must produce a NULQ-FS-002 MEDIUM finding.

scenarios.title: App scan kernel findings accounted
scenarios.description: Kernel findings in the app scan are allowed but not asserted; no filesystem findings are expected under /lab/fixtures/app.

scenarios.title: File capability metadata unsupported in lab
scenarios.reason: Setting real security.capability xattrs on fixture binaries requires capabilities not available in the read-only laboratory image.

scenarios.title: Sudoers policy parsing unsupported in lab
scenarios.reason: The sudo collector reads /etc/sudoers from the live system, not from --root fixtures.

scenarios.title: Cron job inventory unsupported in lab
scenarios.reason: The cron collector reads system cron directories from the live system, not from --root fixtures.

scenarios.title: systemd unit analysis unsupported in lab
scenarios.reason: Alpine does not run systemd; no service is started or stopped.

scenarios.title: Container runtime configuration unsupported in lab
scenarios.reason: Deeper container runtime configuration analysis is scheduled for M4; no container escape is attempted.
